title: Market Tilt & Model Signal Catalog: Field Research Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable playbook and lightweight data catalog for continuous market-level signals that matter to Redwood Inference customers: latency economics, quantization compatibility, model availability, feature parity (streaming, function-calling), and enterprise controls. The deliverable is a scoped playbook, signal taxonomy, initial probe plan (6 week), telemetry queries, and a scoring rubric so PMs and Solutions can prioritise onboarding & fallback decisions.
objective: Deliver a practical ops-ready catalog of competitive signals and a field research playbook that converts qualitative scouting into quantitative prioritization for model onboarding and fallback rules.
success_metrics: Signal catalog prototype covering >=12 model vendors/variants
Automated telemetry queries producing weekly availability and latency deltas for top-6 models
Scoring rubric validated with 3 internal product/solutions use-cases
Playbook used by 2 customer-facing pilots (Solutions/SE) within 6 weeks
scope_in_scope: Define 10 core signal categories (latency, tail latencies, token cost, quant-compat, KV-cache friendliness, streaming support, tool-calling match, deployment compatibility, E2E privacy/compliance footprints, documentation/ops maturity)
Author telemetry query templates for latency, success-rate, and error-mode signals (retrospective and synthetic probes)
Create a simple 0-100 scoring rubric and prioritization matrix
Pack playbook as a 1-page quickstart + 6-step field guide for Solutions and PMs
out_of_scope: Deep model quality evals (LLM behavior evaluation beyond basic regressions)
tasks: Finalize signal taxonomy draft and publish to Confluence
Run synthetic probe harness across 12 candidate model endpoints (hosted and partner endpoints)
Instrument latency and availability dashboards (Console -> custom temporary dashboard)
Draft scoring rubric and map to product decisions (fallback, reserved capacity, quantization recommendation)
Interview 5 Solutions/SEs for real-world prioritization criteria
Run two customer-facing micro-probes (one fintech, one SaaS search) to validate rubric signal weights
Produce playbook artifacts: 1-pager, Confluence doc, telemetry queries repo, and an internal demo slide deck
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with signal taxonomy and example telemetry queries
Probe harness produces a reproducible weekly CSV for top-12 models
Scoring rubric documented and applied to at least 3 real model variants with decision recommendations
Stakeholder review (Solutions, Applied ML, Observability) completed and sign-off recorded
risks: Telemetry coverage gap: some third-party endpoints block synthetic probing
Signal noise: short-run probes may produce misleading latency tails
Cross-team bandwidth: Observability or Infra capacity to create dashboards may be constrained
mitigations: Fallback to partner-reported metrics and public SLAs when probes are blocked
Use controlled synthetic traffic with variable sequence lengths and warm caches to stabilise signals
Reserve a 2-day observability sprint in the sprint plan and re-use existing dashboard templates
